author: Evagrius Ponticus
occasion: A collection of brief spiritual maxims arranged by initial letter, intended for monastic formation and moral instruction.
argument: The work offers short, memorable sayings on the spiritual life, arranged alphabetically in Greek. It teaches that salvation begins with self-condemnation, that virtue must be practiced in deeds rather than words, and that the soul must be purified from passions. The maxims contrast true piety, friendship, and wisdom with their counterfeits such as vainglory, pride, and love of pleasure. The final sayings focus on knowledge of God, humility, and union with Christ through keeping his commandments.

outline.move: Opening alphabetical sayings on self-knowledge, speech, justice, piety, friendship, and the dangers of the passions.
Further sayings on knowing God through self-knowledge, true friendship, the soul's nobility, and the stranger and poor as God's eye-salve.
Sayings on beneficence, rhetoric, self-control and gentleness as Cherubim, honor in old age, true contemplation, love, friendship, purity of soul, and the dangers of self-love.

Closing sayings on self-knowledge, vainglory, pride, Scripture, tears, humility, the virtuous man as paradise tree, Christ as the tree of life, feeding the poor to feed Christ, eating Christ's body, keeping commandments, the friend who flows with milk and honey, the pleasure-loving mind as harsh master, burying truth, and the fear of God.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
cast.who: The Son of God, presented as the tree of life, the one whose body is eaten and commandments are kept, and the source from whom the friend according to God flows with milk and honey.

key_terms.sense: Virtue or excellence of soul, to be practiced in deed and taught in word.
The soul, the inner person that must be purified and nourished.
The passions or disordered desires that enslave the soul.
Vainglorious or love of empty honor, a disease of the soul.
Proud or arrogant, a disposition that destroys virtue.
Humility or lowliness of mind, an unbreakable weapon for the soul.
Contemplation or true spiritual vision, the upper room of the soul.
Almsgiving or mercy shown to the poor, which smooths the way.
Self-love, the root that hates all things.
The commandments of Christ, which the one who loves him keeps.
The Scriptures, ignorance of which is a serious error for a true man.
Cherubim, angelic beings symbolizing the soul's self-control and gentleness.

scripture: The work uses standard Greek Christian terminology for Scripture (αἱ Γραφαί) without explicit book citations. No LXX or Vulgate book names or Psalm numbering appear in the text.
uncertain: The precise date of composition within Evagrius's lifetime.
Whether the work was originally addressed to a specific monastic community or individual.
The original title may have varied in manuscript tradition.
